By requirement, all users must be treated equally regarding pricing, how rates are developed must be documented, rates must be transparent to all users, only directly attributable and trackable costs can be included in rate development, and rates must be set for cost recovery, not profit. 8 The following is most applicable: Cost Principles for Educational Institutions OMB Circular A-21 (2 CFR Part 220), http://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/circulars_a021_2004/ Final Technical Report 54/57 14.7.1 Cost of Ownership Recovery The initial strategy to recover the cost of ownership expense would be to develop a daily rate that is accrued when MTV is reserved for user use (equivalent to an indirect rate for MTV activities). This approach requires estimating non-user utilization and user utilization days based on the best available a priori information related to user project timing (including regulatory approvals, user readiness, contracting, etc.) and diligent recording/scheduling of maintenance. Days when the MTV is in modes: Stand-by (not reserved for user use), Maintenance, and Out of Service must be estimated and will not be available to recover costs using the daily recovery rate. As with other recharge cost centers managed by FAU, full cost recovery is a goal that is rarely achieved. Rather, the activities supported by FAU cost centers are deemed highly valuable to the university and likely to be supported regardless of actual cost recovery. Therefore, university recharge cost centers typically aim for at least a 40% recovery of actual costs. In the case of the MTV, the goal would be to collect minimum not-in-use fixed costs to ensure fiscal sustainability. Assuming 30 annual days were reserved for maintenance activities when the MTV would not be available to users and utilizing the estimated cost of ownership developed, a daily rate calculation was developed. The MTV would then have to be used for 117 days annually to recover not-in-use fixed costs and for 134 days annually to achieve a minimum 40% recovery, approximately a third of every year. Rate setting this way is often more of an art than a science, especially for first attempts. However, during each year of ownership, data from previous years can be used to optimize a balance between user affordability and cost recovery. 14.7.2 Cost of Operation Recovery The strategy to recover costs of operation expenses would be to allocate non-FAU costs to the user and provide not-to-exceed FAU cost proposals before performance for directly billed effort and other expenses (e.g., travel). Planning and regulatory costs will be estimated during initial engagement with the prospective MTV user. Once a plan, authorizations, and commitment are in place for MTV use, a separate estimate will be developed, including FAU and direct MTV user costs. Depending upon the duration of MTV utilization, FAU costs may be billed to the MTV user monthly, quarterly, or on a different collectively agreed-upon schedule.
